title: Oxycodone after knee replacement; a single preoperative gabapentin dose is not a combination

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved 2026-11-16 (#200) at 0.1.1 and re-confirmed 2026-11-16 (#202) at 0.2.0 with the senna order added in #201, so the case tests only the opioid with a sedative rule. The basis is the label text quoted in #198, read by Claude Code on DailyMed; the owner did not report reading the labels.

story: A 70-year-old man has an elective right total knee arthroplasty. As part of the enhanced recovery pathway he receives one dose of gabapentin 300 mg on the evening before surgery, with no further gabapentin ordered. After surgery he has oxycodone 5 mg by mouth every 4 hours as needed and scheduled acetaminophen. On the first postoperative morning only the oxycodone and acetaminophen are active.

problems.title: Presence of right artificial knee joint

prescriptions.instructions: 300 mg by mouth once, the evening before surgery (enhanced recovery pathway)
5 mg by mouth every 4 hours as needed for pain
17.2 mg (2 tablets) by mouth at bedtime

reference_answer: No change for this rule: the single preoperative gabapentin dose has ended, so oxycodone is the only CNS depressant now ordered. Continue multimodal analgesia and the usual postoperative monitoring.
rationale: A near miss for the opioid with a sedative rule: gabapentin is on the chart, but as one preoperative dose that ended before the newest charted day. The rule reads orders active on that day and must stay silent.

citations.supports: 5.8: the risk is from gabapentin coadministered with opioids; a dose that has ended is not coadministration. Read in the label by Claude Code; owner approved 2026-11-16 (#200).
